notes:
I've put together notes on 2 Corinthians 9 from about a dozen sources, but there are some gaps. I ran out of searches and page reads before I could look at the NET Bible notes, Ligonier, the Lutheran and Methodist sites, Pentecostal denominational sources, Orthodox sources, or the full Ellicott and Pulpit commentaries. The Precept Austin page cut off after verse 1, so its notes on later verses come only from search snippets. Chrysostom's homily on verses 10–15 is not covered either.

On the traditions question: I found only two places where the sources really disagree. One is what "righteousness" means in v. 9. The other is how far v. 6 promises earthly reward, which matters for the prosperity debate. I did not find tradition-specific disagreement on other verses.

---

**v. 1**
- **Traditional reading.** Paul may be gently teasing here. In effect he says he doesn't even need to remind them, because they are already willing to give. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/ It also shows he is done persuading them, as he did in chapter 8. Now he is coaching them on *how* to give. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **The chapter break.** The Pulpit Commentary, quoted on Precept Austin, says the opening "for" shows Paul is still on the same subject. On that reading, chapter 9 is not a separate letter or fragment. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Catholic/Orthodox (Chrysostom, a Church Father).** He sees skill in Paul calling it "superfluous" to write and then writing about it anyway. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm
- **Modern scholarship.** Bible Odyssey describes the collection as a fund Paul raised for Jewish Christians in Jerusalem. https://www.bibleodyssey.org/dictionary/collection-for-the-saints/

**v. 2**
- **Traditional reading.** Guzik (Enduring Word) reads the boast to the Macedonians as a "playful" nudge. Paul seems to be saying, "I've already bragged about you." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Matthew Henry.** By praising what they had done, Paul put them under an obligation to keep going. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Cr/2Cr_009.cfm
- **Precept Austin.** The Corinthians' zeal fired the Macedonians up to copy them, but stirring others to give is not the same as giving. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Chrysostom.** Paul doesn't tell them to imitate the Macedonians. He tells them the Macedonians imitated *them*, so the teachers must not fall behind their pupils. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm

**v. 3**
- **Traditional reading.** Guzik hears a light, playful tone again. Paul is sure they would bring the gift, but he is sending the brothers to collect it anyway. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Matthew Henry.** Giving advance notice meant they wouldn't be caught out by hasty demands. When we want others to do good, we should treat them wisely and give them time. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Cr/2Cr_009.cfm

**v. 4**
- **Traditional reading.** Guzik paraphrases it as: you don't want the Macedonians to see you were unwilling. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Chrysostom.** The shame grows with the number of onlookers. He notes Paul says "unprepared," not "unwilling." If being slow is a disgrace, think how much worse it is to give nothing, or less than you should. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm

**v. 5**
- **Traditional reading.** Paul wanted the collection finished before he arrived, so that nothing about receiving it could look manipulative. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/ Biblical generosity is more about attitude than amount. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Chrysostom.** Paul wanted them to give both much *and* freely. A gift given unwillingly is really something taken by force. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm

**v. 6**
- **Traditional reading.** Giving is like sowing seed. What you give isn't lost, and it carries the power of life and growth. But Paul is talking about the *quality* of giving, not the quantity. (Constable, quoting Hughes) https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-corinthians/9-6.html
- **Calvin (Reformed).** He compares almsgiving to seed that is scattered, buried and seems to rot, so that it looks lost. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-corinthians/9-6.html Quoted on Precept Austin, Calvin says the harvest means both eternal life and earthly blessing: God rewards the godly "in this world as well." https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Adam Clarke (Methodist).** He calls it a plain rule: no one can expect to reap more than he sowed. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-corinthians/9-6.html
- **John Gill (Baptist).** If you give nothing, you reap nothing. If you are generous with earthly goods, you will prosper in the same kind. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/erv2-corinthians/9-6.html
- **Guzik.** The principle works both spiritually and materially: "you can't out-give God." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Chrysostom.** Paul calls giving "sowing" so that we think of the harvest and feel we receive more than we give. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm
- **Prosperity teaching (debated).** Sam Storms (TGC) says he has heard prosperity-gospel preachers use this verse. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/paul-teach-prosperity-gospel/ He answers that the reaping isn't for building personal wealth. It is so believers can be even more generous. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/paul-teach-prosperity-gospel/

**v. 7**
- **Traditional reading.** Every Christian should give, even those who can't give much. Giving should never be forced or manipulated. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/ God himself is the ultimate cheerful giver. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Matthew Henry.** Giving should be planned and deliberate, not done on impulse. Otherwise people give more than they meant to under pressure, then regret it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Cr/2Cr_009.cfm
- **Chrysostom.** People act more readily when left free than when compelled. He adds that what is done under compulsion loses its reward. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm

**v. 8**
- **Traditional reading.** Guzik says God blesses giving in many ways, materially and spiritually. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/ He reads the Greek word for "sufficiency" (*autarkeia*, contentment) as a cure for materialism. We are blessed to be "channels," not "reservoirs." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Precept Austin.** Notice how many times "all" appears (all… always… all… every). https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Chrysostom.** Paul is answering the fear "I'll end up poor." He asks for *enough* in earthly things but *abundance* in spiritual things. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm
- **Storms.** God won't move you to give and then fail to give you what you need to do it. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/paul-teach-prosperity-gospel/

**v. 9** (one of the two real disagreements: what "righteousness" means)
- **Evangelical (Precept Austin).** The quote is from Psalm 112:9. "Righteousness endures forever" points to an eternal reward. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary It firmly denies that giving earns righteousness. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary It rejects the view that the word only means "right living," preferring righteousness credited by God. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Matthew Henry.** Here "righteousness" means almsgiving, whose honour lasts and whose reward is eternal. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Cr/2Cr_009.cfm
- **Expositor's Bible.** In the Psalm, the phrase is God's verdict on a good man's whole character. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/teb/2-corinthians-9.html
- **Catholic/Orthodox (Chrysostom).** "Righteousness" here means love toward others, which "makes righteous, consuming sins like a fire." This contrasts with the evangelical denial above. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/220219.htm

**v. 10**
- **Traditional reading.** God is the great supplier. Whatever we give, he gave us first. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Matthew Henry.** He reads it as a prayer that the Corinthians would always have enough, and that their "seed" would multiply so they could do more good. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Cr/2Cr_009.cfm

**v. 11**
- **Traditional reading.** They are enriched for generous giving, "not for their own riches or lavish lifestyles." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Precept Austin.** The grammar implies God keeps on enriching them. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Storms.** Paul treats wealth as a means to further generosity, not an end in itself. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/paul-teach-prosperity-gospel/

**vv. 12–14**
- **Traditional reading.** The thanks would be for more than the money. People would praise God for the Corinthians' obedience to the gospel and their generous sharing. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Got Questions.** The gift would prove their love was sincere. https://www.gotquestions.org/indescribable-gift.html
- **Precept Austin on the word "proof" (*dokimē*).** It pictures metal that has come through fire and is shown to be genuine. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-corinthians-9-commentary
- **Modern scholarship.** Bible Odyssey says the collection stood for Jews and Gentiles as partners in the gospel. https://www.bibleodyssey.org/dictionary/collection-for-the-saints/ A Themelios review of David Downs's book on the collection reports his view that Paul presents the collection as an act of worship to God. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/themelios/review/the-offering-of-the-gentiles-pauls-collection-for-jerusalem-in-its-chronolo/ Downs rejects the common idea that it was meant to fulfil the prophecies of nations bringing gifts to Zion. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/themelios/review/the-offering-of-the-gentiles-pauls-collection-for-jerusalem-in-its-chronolo/

**v. 15**
- **Traditional reading.** Alford, following Chrysostom, says the gift can only be Jesus Christ himself. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_corinthians/9-15.htm Barnes notes the Greek word for "indescribable" appears nowhere else in the New Testament. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_corinthians/9-15.htm
- **Guzik.** Is it salvation or Christ? He answers, "Why not both?" https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-corinthians-9/
- **Spurgeon (Baptist).** Christ is a gift, he is indescribable, and he calls out our praise. https://www.spurgeon.org/resource-library/sermons/gods-unspeakable-gift/
- **A minority view.** A sermon collection on Bible Hub notes that some expositors take the gift to be the generous spirit God worked in the Corinthians. The excerpt cuts off before saying more. https://biblehub.com/sermons/2_corinthians/9-15.htm
